label: Paris Talks Halt Bombing in October
detail: Negotiations in Paris produce a breakthrough in October and the bombing of North Vietnam ends before Election Day.
assumption: Voters on the context date know the bombing has stopped and that serious negotiations are under way, which weakens the Vietnam issue against the party of the administration in office since 1961 and softens the case for a harder line.
facts_text: On 31 October the President announced that all bombing of North Vietnam would stop the next day, following progress in the Paris talks.
Representatives of the Saigon government and the National Liberation Front have been invited to take part in broadened negotiations.
Officials say the pause rests on an understanding that the talks will proceed promptly and that North Vietnam will respect the demilitarized zone.

add_planks.text: Continue the Paris negotiations toward a settlement of the war, with the bombing of North Vietnam halted.

research_questions: How did voters' support for the party of the administration in office shift after the 31 October 1968 announcement of the bombing halt?
How did voters who ranked Vietnam as their top issue split in late October 1968 compared with September?
Did late-deciding voters in 1968 move toward the party in power when peace seemed near?
source_text: Peace talks in Paris break through in October 1968 and the bombing of North Vietnam stops before Election Day.
